title: Bisecting a broken graph: previews are your print statement

questions.q: In a chain of 16 nodes, how many previews does halving need at most?
questions.why: Each check halves what's left. The lab gives 4.

questions.q: Your probe at the middle looks right. What now?
options: The fault is later, so check the middle of the second half
questions.answer: The fault is later, so check the middle of the second half
questions.why: Clean here means everything before it is fine.

questions.q: Why fix the seed while hunting a fault?
questions.why: With a random seed the picture differs on each run, which hides what your change did.

questions.q: PreviewAny prints a 64 by 64 latent with one NaN in the middle. Will you see nan?
options: No: the middle is summarised as ...
questions.answer: No: the middle is summarised as ...
questions.why: Torch shortens big tensors. The lab shows it.

questions.q: What is the first bad node?
options: The last node in the graph
The one whose input looks right and whose output doesn't
The one with the most wires
questions.answer: The one whose input looks right and whose output doesn't

questions.q: Why does wiring a preview to a node with no outputs make it run?
options: A preview is an output node, so its branch is needed
questions.answer: A preview is an output node, so its branch is needed
questions.why: The engine walks back from output nodes.
